headline: Profit jumps on broad trading and dealmaking strength
summary_short: Citigroup's Q2 2026 net income rose 45% y/y (1% q/q) to $5,831M as revenue climbed 14% y/y to $24,766M and diluted EPS jumped 61% y/y to $3.15, powered by broad growth across Services, Markets, and Banking plus a lower provision for credit losses.
summary_long: Revenue grew 14% y/y to $24,766M on growth across all five businesses plus FX translation, partly offset by weaker Corporate/Other; net interest income rose 13% and non-interest revenue rose 18%. Operating expenses rose 5% y/y on higher compensation, transactional/product-servicing costs, and deposit insurance, but fell 1% q/q. Net income jumped 45% y/y to $5,831M as revenue growth and a 12% y/y drop in loan-loss provisions outpaced expense growth; RoTCE rose to 13.0% from 8.7% and the efficiency ratio improved to 57.4% from 62.7%. CET1 held at 12.8%, helped by the Banamex stake sale, while book value per share rose 7% y/y to $114.74. Citi also raised its dividend 12% and launched a $30B buyback.

drivers.explanation: Growth across each of Citi's five interconnected businesses and Legacy Franchises, plus FX translation, partially offset by a decline in Corporate/Other; net interest income +13%, non-interest revenue +18%.
Higher compensation and benefits, transactional and product-servicing expenses, and deposit insurance costs, plus FX translation, partially offset by lower professional-services expenses.
A smaller net ACL build ($118M) driven by portfolio growth and macro-variable changes, largely offset by portfolio-quality improvements including seasonal changes in USCC.
Higher revenues and a lower provision for credit losses more than offset higher operating expenses.
EPS grew faster than net income y/y (61% vs 45%) because share repurchases reduced the diluted share count.

Quarter-over-quarter increase driven by net income, the net impact of Citi's sale of a 22.6% equity stake in Banamex, and lower deferred tax assets, partially offset by buybacks, dividends, and higher risk-weighted assets.

CEO Fraser cited the best quarterly revenue in a decade, record Services revenue with over 30% returns, 45% growth in Equities, 34% growth in Banking, and announced a 12% dividend increase plus a $30B share-buyback plan.
